Mini INMO

This is a short practice paper modelled on the Indian National Mathematical Olympiad (INMO). The real INMO has six problems of 17 marks each (102 in total) and lasts about four and a half hours. This mini paper has four problems in 3 hours: one each from algebra, number theory, combinatorics and geometry.

  • All problems are proof-based. A correct final answer alone earns very little. You must give a complete, rigorous justification of every claim.
  • Each problem carries 17 marks. Partial credit is given for substantial progress, so write down your key ideas even if your solution is incomplete.
  • No calculators, computers or other aids. The syllabus is pre-calculus: no calculus is needed.
  • Type your solutions with the Math tool. Write prose with LaTeX between dollar signs, for example $a^2+b^2\ge 2ab$.
  • For diagrams, use the geometry tool (geometry problems) or the isometric grid tool (lattice problems). A diagram is not a proof: state and justify everything in words.
  • You may work on the problems in any order and move freely between them. The notes pad is available for rough work and is not marked.

The exam is proctored. Stay in full-screen mode and do not switch tabs. Good luck!
